# Tools

Use this page when you need the practical path for callable tools: define the
tool, test it, wire it into a workflow or assistant surface, and understand the
sandbox and approval boundaries.

## At a glance

| Task | Start here | Deep reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| define or register a tool | shape the callable contract first | [Tools architecture](m-03-tools.md) |
| verify tool behavior | use fixture-backed tests | [Tools architecture](m-03-tools.md) |
| call the tool from a workflow | connect it through a workflow node | [Workflows](m-42-use-workflows.md) |
| govern side effects | inspect approval and runtime policy boundaries | [Trust and governance](m-33-trust-and-governance.md) |

## The tool journey, step by step

This is the loop the alpha supports end to end for a tool, with each step as a page action.
`caliber/caliber-ui/e2e/tool-journey.spec.ts` drives it on the shipped defaults (it saves the fixtures and creates
the workflow through the API, the endpoints the page's editors save to).

| # | Step | In the page (Tools) | What you should see |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Register | **Register Tool**, then the wizard: name, module, callable, input schema | the tool's workspace (`/tools?tool=TL-…`, an address a reload keeps) |
| 2 | Run it | **Sandbox**, then **Test Run**, with a JSON object as input (anything else is refused with a message, not run) | the tool's output, produced by the sandbox |
| 3 | Save fixtures | open the tool, **Fixtures**: add cases with an input and an assertion | the cases are saved against the tool |
| 4 | Calibrate | **Fixtures**: **Run calibration** | "Pass rate 100% — 2/2 passed", or which cases failed |
| 5 | Pin a baseline | **Test Runs**: **Set as baseline** on a run (a run is saved when you invoke the tool on **Sandbox** or run the suite on **Hardening**) | the run carries a **Baseline** marker, and later runs are compared to it |
| 6 | Use it in a workflow | reference the tool from an agent node in a workflow version | the workflow appears under **Publish**, **Where used** |
| 7 | Make a new version | **Publish**, **Version history**, **New version** (admins): the wizard opens on the tool with its name fixed and the version one on; change what differs and register | the new version's own workspace; the history lists both versions, and you can promote or roll back between them |

Two things about the Tools list. A fresh install lists sixteen tools that CALIBER seeded itself, and each
is labelled **Built-in**, so you can tell them from the ones an admin registered. Four of them are the
agent-memory tools (`memory_search`, `memory_list`, `list_entities`, `memory_add`). While agent memory is
off (`CALIBER_MEMORY_ENABLED` is not `true`) they are labelled **Unavailable**, with the reason on the
row, because wiring one into a workflow would only make it return an error at run time.

## Who is trusted to write tools

Read this before you let anyone register a tool.

- **Tool authors are trusted.** A registered tool is code, imported from a Python module and called. Only a
  global admin can register, change or archive a tool, and that is the whole of the trust model: CALIBER
  does not defend itself against an admin who registers a malicious tool.
- **The sandbox is a process boundary, not a container.** By default each call runs in a separate Python
  interpreter with an empty environment, a private working directory, resource limits and a wall-clock
  deadline that kills the process group. It is **not** a container, virtual machine or seccomp boundary:
  the child keeps ambient filesystem and network access on the host. That is appropriate for tool authors
  you trust and is not isolation from ones you do not. Set `CALIBER_TOOL_SANDBOX_BACKEND` to a backend you
  provide if you need OS-enforced isolation. Without one, promoting a workflow version that uses registered
  tools to a production-class alias is refused: `CALIBER_TOOL_SANDBOX_REQUIRE_EXTERNAL_ISOLATION_FOR_ENVIRONMENT_CLASSES`
  defaults to `production` (set it empty to turn the gate off), and an alias whose name is not recognised as
  staging or development counts as production.
- **Restrict which modules a tool may come from.** `CALIBER_REGISTERED_TOOL_MODULE_ALLOWLIST` is a
  comma-separated list of module prefixes, for example `caliber.*,mycompany.tools.*`. It ships empty, which
  means any importable module may be registered, and `/readiness` reports that as "registered tool modules
  are unrestricted" (a check that is not required, so it never fails readiness). Set it for anything beyond a
  local trial.
- **Inside a project, roles apply on top of that.** Registering, changing or archiving a tool needs
  `caliber.admin` and, for a project tool, `editor` or `owner`; saving fixtures needs `editor` or `owner`.
  Running a tool, starting a calibration, recording a test run and setting a baseline need `reviewer`, `editor`
  or `owner`, and each of those also needs `caliber.operator`. Reading needs only membership. A member
  whose role is too weak gets 403 and a person outside the project gets 404. See
  [Auth and project scoping](m-31-auth-and-project-scoping.md).
- **Side effects need approval.** A tool that writes or acts on an external system is registered with
  approval required, and the sandbox mocks it in preview runs.
- **Workflows add a second boundary of the same kind.** A `python_code` node is authorable by operators.
  Preview refuses it and a published run blocks `import`, but that is containment, not isolation.

## 1. What tools are for in CALIBER

Tools are versioned callable assets. They are not just snippets attached to a
prompt. CALIBER tracks their contract, tests, and execution boundaries because
they may touch real external systems.

## 2. Common tasks

| You want to... | Read this next |
| --- | --- |

## 3. Common failure modes

| Symptom | First thing to check |
| --- | --- |
| The tool works locally but not in CALIBER | packaging, sandbox assumptions, or missing dependencies |
| The tool appears but cannot run live | approval policy or runtime permission boundary |
| The workflow compiles but the tool step fails | tool schema/inputs do not match the runtime call shape |
